title: The World's Longest Sea Crossing Is 55 km — Then It Dives Underwater | China Travel Expert
description:
Imagine driving across the ocean for 55 kilometres — then watching the road ahead disappear beneath the waves.

The Hong Kong–Zhuhai–Macau Bridge is the world's longest sea crossing: a 55 km bridge-island-tunnel system across the Pearl River estuary that ties Hong Kong to Zhuhai and Macau. Its main span runs about 29.6 km, but the clever part is the middle — a 6.7 km immersed tunnel that dips as deep as 50 m under the sea so giant container ships can sail straight over the top. Two artificial islands are what let drivers transition from bridge to tunnel and back. It turned a multi-hour ferry trip around the delta into a drive of well under an hour.

🧭 Expert Tip: You can't just drive your own car across — private access is tightly capped. Tourists take the cross-border shuttle bus between the Hong Kong and Zhuhai/Macau ports; buy a ticket at the port and bring your passport/permit.
